5. Incremental Fine-Tuning¶

Retrain an existing model on new training data (dataset_1 or dataset_2) and demonstrate improvement while keeping evaluation on the same fixed test set.

5. Error Analysis on New Data¶

Predict on the new training dataset to identify incorrect or low-confidence predictions before retraining.

In [8]:
# ── Select the new training dataset ──
NEW_DATASET = "dataset_4"  

new_data_dir = PREPROCESSED_DIR / "train" / NEW_DATASET
new_images = new_data_dir / "images"
new_labels = new_data_dir / "labels"

img_count = len(list(new_images.glob("*.jpg")))
print(f"New dataset   : {NEW_DATASET}")
print(f"Images        : {img_count}")

New dataset   : dataset_4
Images        : 990
In [9]:
# Predict on new data and find low-confidence / missed detections
image_files = sorted(new_images.glob("*.jpg"))
low_conf_images = []

for img_path in image_files:
    results = base_model.predict(str(img_path), imgsz=640, conf=0.25, verbose=False)
    boxes = results[0].boxes

    # Read ground-truth label count
    lbl_path = new_labels / f"{img_path.stem}.txt"
    gt_count = 0
    if lbl_path.exists():
        with open(lbl_path) as f:
            gt_count = sum(1 for line in f if line.strip())

    pred_count = len(boxes) if boxes is not None else 0
    avg_conf = float(boxes.conf.mean()) if boxes is not None and len(boxes) > 0 else 0.0

    if pred_count < gt_count or avg_conf < 0.5:
        low_conf_images.append({
            "image": img_path.name,
            "gt_objects": gt_count,
            "predicted": pred_count,
            "avg_confidence": round(avg_conf, 3),
        })

print(f"Images with low confidence or missed detections: {len(low_conf_images)} / {len(image_files)}")
if low_conf_images:
    display(pd.DataFrame(low_conf_images).head(15))

In [10]:
# Visualize some error samples
if low_conf_images:
    error_names = [e["image"] for e in low_conf_images[:6]]
    cols = min(3, len(error_names))
    rows = (len(error_names) + cols - 1) // cols
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(6 * cols, 5 * rows))
    axes = np.array(axes).flatten() if rows * cols > 1 else np.array([axes])

    for idx, name in enumerate(error_names):
        img_path = new_images / name
        res = base_model.predict(str(img_path), imgsz=640, conf=0.25, verbose=False)
        annotated = res[0].plot()
        axes[idx].imshow(cv2.cvtColor(annotated, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB))
        axes[idx].set_title(name, fontsize=9)
        axes[idx].axis("off")

    for idx in range(len(error_names), len(axes)):
        axes[idx].axis("off")
    plt.suptitle("Error samples — base model on new data", fontsize=13)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("No significant errors found.")

6. Fine-Tuning Configuration¶

Configure the incremental training run. The model is retrained using only the new dataset — no splits, no test data.

In [11]:
# ── Configurable hyperparameters ──
FT_EPOCHS     = 30
FT_BATCH_SIZE = 8
FT_LR         = 0.001
FT_IMG_SIZE   = 640

print(f"Dataset       : {NEW_DATASET}")
print(f"Epochs        : {FT_EPOCHS}")
print(f"Batch size    : {FT_BATCH_SIZE}")
print(f"Learning rate : {FT_LR}")
print(f"Image size    : {FT_IMG_SIZE}")

Epochs        : 30
Batch size    : 8
Learning rate : 0.001

7. Incremental Training¶

Fine-tune the base model on the new training dataset.

In [12]:
# Create YAML for the new dataset
ft_yaml = create_dataset_yaml(NEW_DATASET)

# Load a fresh copy of the base model for training
ft_model = YOLO(str(base_model_path))

ft_results = ft_model.train(
    data=str(ft_yaml),
    epochs=FT_EPOCHS,
    batch=FT_BATCH_SIZE,
    imgsz=FT_IMG_SIZE,
    lr0=FT_LR,
    device=device,
    seed=SEED,
    project=str(RUNS_DIR),
    name=f"{NEW_DATASET}_finetune",
    exist_ok=True,
    verbose=True,
)

ft_best_pt = Path(ft_model.trainer.save_dir) / "weights" / "best.pt"
print(f"\nFine-tuned model: {ft_best_pt}")

8. MLflow Logging¶

Log this fine-tuning run as a new MLflow run. Previous runs are never modified or overwritten.

In [15]:
# Evaluate fine-tuned model on test set
ft_model_eval = YOLO(str(ft_best_pt))
metrics = evaluate_model(ft_model_eval, data_yaml=ft_yaml, img_size=FT_IMG_SIZE)

# Re-establish MLflow connection (falls back to file store if server is down)
setup_mlflow()

with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"finetune_{NEW_DATASET}") as run:
    # Hyperparameters
    mlflow.log_params({
        "base_model_run_id": BASE_RUN_ID,
        "dataset": NEW_DATASET,
        "epochs": FT_EPOCHS,
        "batch_size": FT_BATCH_SIZE,
        "img_size": FT_IMG_SIZE,
        "learning_rate": FT_LR,
        "seed": SEED,
    })

    mlflow.log_metrics(metrics)

    # Model artifact (.pt copy)
    mlflow.log_artifact(str(ft_best_pt), artifact_path="model")

    # YOLO training artifacts (curves, confusion matrices, results)
    ft_save_dir = Path(ft_model.trainer.save_dir)
    log_yolo_run_artifacts(ft_save_dir)

    # Per-epoch training metrics from results.csv
    log_yolo_epoch_metrics(ft_save_dir)

    # Register model in MLflow Model Registry
    register_yolo_model(ft_best_pt, MLFLOW_MODEL_NAME)

    ft_run_id = run.info.run_id

print(f"\nMLflow Run ID : {ft_run_id}")
print(f"Run Name      : finetune_{NEW_DATASET}")

10. Before vs After Comparison¶

Side-by-side comparison of metrics before and after fine-tuning on the same fixed test set.

In [18]:
comparison = pd.DataFrame({
    "Metric": list(pre_metrics.keys()),
    "Before": list(pre_metrics.values()),
    "After": list(metrics.values()),
})
comparison["Delta"] = comparison["After"] - comparison["Before"]
comparison["Improved"] = comparison["Delta"].apply(lambda d: "Yes" if d > 0 else ("No" if d < 0 else "-"))

display(comparison)

# Bar chart
x = np.arange(len(comparison))
width = 0.35
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
ax.bar(x - width / 2, comparison["Before"], width, label="Before")
ax.bar(x + width / 2, comparison["After"], width, label="After")
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(comparison["Metric"], rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_ylabel("Score")
ax.set_title(f"Before vs After — Fine-tuning on {NEW_DATASET}")
ax.legend()
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
